how_it_was_caught: *** BY DOING WHAT WAS ASKED AND FINDING IT ALREADY DONE. *** The claim was written from memory while correcting a different error, which is exactly when this archive has gone wrong before - reaching for a record name to end a paragraph with instead of opening the file.

what_was_said: *** That a seventh daughter, EDITH, born at Bideford in September quarter 1882, fills the gap the name SEPTIMA requires. *** Graded a STRONG CANDIDATE since 16 September, on three legs: the tree's count of ten children, the meaning of Septima, and a single birth-index entry.
what_is_true: *** SHE IS NOT IN THE FAMILY'S BAPTISM REGISTER, and every one of her supposed siblings is. *** Devon Baptisms, Northam St Margaret, archive reference 1843A/PR/1/16: *** SEVEN children of William Taylor and Mary Ann Helen/Ellen *** - Horace Archibald and Isabella Temple (1874), Margaret Helen Walker (1876), Irene (1879), Lucy Elizabeth (31 Aug 1881), *** Mary Septima (30 Oct 1884) *** and Agnes Walker (21 Aug 1889). *** NO EDITH. *** Lucy and Mary Septima sit three years and two months apart with nothing between them, and the candidate falls exactly in that gap. *** AND THE ONLY TWO DEVON EDITHS NEAR THE DATE ARE OTHER PEOPLE: *** Edith Taylor, baptised 21 Nov 1883 at Bideford, mother *** MARIA ***; Edith Mary Taylor, 8 Apr 1885 at Bideford, mother *** ELIZABETH ***. *** THE CANDIDATE IS DOWNGRADED FROM STRONG TO WEAK ***, and what survives is only the tree's unsourced count and the meaning of a name.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY SEARCHING ON THE MOTHER INSTEAD OF THE CHILD, after David asked for the 1891 census. *** One search on 'Mary Ann Helen' returns the whole sibling group at once, which is what makes the absence provable - child-by-child searching could only ever have failed to find her. *** THE CONTROL WAS RUN FIRST: *** Agnes Walker Taylor, whose birth this archive had to the day and the address, was looked for before anything else and is there. *** AND IT STRENGTHENS DAVID'S OWN READING OF THE PHOTOGRAPH *** - if there is no eighth daughter, the eighth woman in the group is not a daughter, and his grandmother or aunt is the better explanation.

what_was_said: *** That William Taylor and Mary Ann Hellen Brayley had TEN children, and that a tenth is missing. *** Taken from a MyHeritage tree that names nine and asserts ten, and carried on /taylor/ under a *** Documented *** chip. It has driven three weeks of searching: work-list rows 126, 127, 128, 192 and 193, a FreeBMD death sweep, a FreeREG attempt, a findmypast baptism search and two candidate children.
what_is_true: *** THERE ARE NINE, AND NOTHING IS MISSING. *** The GRO's own index, which prints the mother's maiden surname, was searched for TAYLOR births with mother BRAYLEY across *** 1870-1893, both sexes, ten windows ***: *** Kathleen Georgina (1870 D, 05B/490), William John (1870 D, 05B/489), Horace Archibald (1872 J, 05B/507), Isabella Temple (1874 D, 05B/497), Margaret Hellen Walker (1876 D, 05B/481), Irene (1879 M, 05B/524), Lucy Elizabeth (1881 S, 05B/508), MARY SEPTIMA (1884 D, 05B/506) and Agnes Walker (1889 S, 05B/502). *** All at BIDEFORD. Nothing before, nothing between, nothing after.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY DAVID LOGGING THIS SESSION IN TO gro.gov.uk *** and the search row 128 had named in September being run at last. *** THE INDEX ANSWERS BY DEFINITION RATHER THAN BY INFERENCE: *** FreeBMD's birth index carries no mother's maiden name, so no amount of work there could ever have joined a Bideford Taylor child to this household - which row 128 said in terms and was right about. *** AND THE CRITICAL WINDOW WAS RE-RUN ON LOOSE SPELLING MATCHING *** because this archive has documented BRAILEY as a variant: 28 births across England, the same two at Bideford.

what_was_said: *** That EDITH Taylor (Bideford, Sep q 1882) and ETHEL Taylor (Bideford, Dec q 1882) were candidates for the missing daughter, and that an unnamed TWIN OF IRENE, 1879, was the fifth daughter. *** Edith was graded a STRONG CANDIDATE on 16 September; Ethel was called the better fit on 17 September; the twin has been on /taylor/ since the beginning, inferred to be female *** 'or the arithmetic does not come out'. ***
what_is_true: *** ALL THREE ARE GONE. *** Neither Edith nor Ethel has BRAYLEY as her mother in the GRO index, so neither is a child of this couple. And *** IRENE IS ALONE IN 1879 ***: no second birth to this mother that year, of either sex. *** The twin was never a person. She was an arithmetical requirement wearing a tree's silence as evidence ***, and this archive built her, published her, and reasoned from her.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY ASKING THE ONE INDEX THAT CAN REFUSE AN ANSWER. *** Every earlier search could only fail to find a child; this one can show she is not there, because it is keyed on the mother. *** THE BAPTISM REGISTER HAD ALREADY POINTED THIS WAY *** hours earlier - seven children at Northam, no Edith, no Ethel, Irene alone in 1879 - and the GRO settled it.

what_was_said: *** That SEPTIMA means seventh and that the name is therefore a count of daughters - 'her own name is a piece of arithmetic, and it turns out to be exactly right'. *** The founding observation of /taylor/, and the reason the tenth child was ever looked for.
what_is_true: *** MARY SEPTIMA IS THE SIXTH DAUGHTER AND THE EIGHTH CHILD, and no reading of the registered family makes her seventh of anything. *** Daughters in order: Kathleen (1), Isabella (2), Margaret (3), Irene (4), Lucy (5), *** Mary Septima (6) ***, Agnes (7). *** THE NAME IS NOW AN UNEXPLAINED FACT RATHER THAN AN ARITHMETICAL ONE ***, which is a worse answer and a truer one. *** ONE CATEGORY OF CHILD LEAVES NO BIRTH REGISTRATION AT ALL: *** a stillbirth, which was *** not registrable in England and Wales until 1927 ***. A seventh pregnancy carried to term and lost would be invisible to every index this archive can reach, and would still be counted by the woman who bore her. *** THAT IS A POSSIBILITY, NOT A FINDING ***, and it is recorded as the shape of the remaining doubt rather than as its answer.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY FINISHING THE COUNT INSTEAD OF DEFENDING IT. *** The arithmetic was never checked against a complete list of children, because no complete list existed until today.

what_was_said: *** That John Walker Brayley was born at ST PANCRAS (the 1851 census) or at ST PAUL'S (the tree), and that his birth year was unresolved between the tree's 1845 and a death index implying 1847. *** data/1851-bideford-brayley.tsv left the parish disagreement open in terms.
what_is_true: *** HIS BIRTH IS REGISTERED IN THE HOLBORN UNION, June quarter 1845, Volume 02 page 149 *** - indexed as *** BRAILEY, JOHN WALKER ***, mother TEMPLE. *** THE YEAR IS SETTLED FOR THE TREE: *** a birth on 22 June 1845 falls in the June quarter, so the 1900 death index that made him 53 had a careless informant - which this archive had already concluded from the census. *** THE PARISH DISPUTE RESOLVES TO NEITHER SIDE: *** the district is HOLBORN, which is also where his sister *** ISABELLA *** was born - the 1861 census enters her as 'London (City), ST ANDREW', that is St Andrew Holborn. *** AND HIS MIDDLE NAME IS WALKER ***, which pushes this family's naming discipline a full generation earlier than the archive had documented it: Temple and Walker were being used as forenames in 1845, not first in 1874.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY SEARCHING FOR THE MOTHER INSTEAD OF THE CHILD, in the GRO's own index. *** The search was run to settle a different question entirely - whether Mary Ann Hellen Brayley has a birth registration - and he came back with it.

what_was_said: *** That MARY ANN HELLEN BRAYLEY's birth registration is merely NOT YET FOUND. *** data/brayley-bmd.tsv recorded on 14 September that FreeBMD holds no Mary Brayley and no Mary Brailey in the June quarter of 1843 anywhere in England and Wales, with the control passed - and left it as an absence awaiting a better search.
what_is_true: *** SHE WAS ALMOST CERTAINLY NEVER REGISTERED, and the archive should stop looking. *** The GRO's own index was searched on *** her MOTHER's maiden surname, TEMPLE, with the child's surname on loose matching, across 1838-1852, both sexes ***. It returns exactly two children of this couple: *** JOHN WALKER (1845, Holborn) and GEORGINA MARGARET (1850, Bideford) ***. *** THE TWO EARLIEST CHILDREN ARE BOTH ABSENT *** - Isabella, about 1841, and Mary Ann Hellen, 20 May 1843, both born in London - *** and the two later ones are both present. *** Birth registration was not compulsory on parents until the Act of 1874, in force from 1875; under-registration in the 1840s is well attested among the urban poor; and the 1851 census describes this household as *** 'Shoemaker Wife Pauper'. *** The null is now double and arrives from two directions - FreeBMD under her own name, the GRO under her mother's.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY ASKING A DIFFERENT QUESTION OF A DIFFERENT INDEX. *** Searching for a person who may not be in a book can only ever fail; searching for her PARENTS returns the children who ARE there, and the shape of who is missing. *** AND THE SPELLING CONTROL IS BUILT IN: *** the query said BRAYLEY and the index returned BRAILEY twice, so the nulls are not a spelling artefact.

Two are this family and new: *** ROQUE LUIS ARMANDO LERENA on a Union voters' roll 1925-1931, polling district 770 ***, and *** NUNO FERNANDO LERENA in a land record, identified by his exact birth date 6.10.1924 ***. *** WHAT SURVIVES OF THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: *** there is no Cape civil registration in the corpus, so row 106 still gains nothing - but for a different reason than the one given.

what_was_said: *** That the Montevideo MARRIAGE DISPENSATION RECORDS are worth opening because they name a groom's PARENTS. *** Written into work-list row 194 yesterday, quoting this archive's own canelones-films.tsv: 'the pre-marriage investigation is worth MORE than the act - it routinely gives a Spanish groom's PARENTS.'
what_is_true: *** TRUE OF THE EXPEDIENTE, NOT OF THIS BOOK. *** The Arquidiocesis de Montevideo Marriage Dispensation Records are the Vicar General's *** SUMMARY LEDGER *** - one sentence per couple, recording whom he dispensed and from what. *** NOT ONE OF THE NINE LERENA ENTRIES READ TODAY NAMES A PARENT. *** The informaciones matrimoniales are a different series, and two record classes were conflated because both are called dispensations in English. *** AND THE LEDGER IS STILL WORTH MORE THAN EXPECTED, FOR A DIFFERENT REASON: *** a consanguinity dispensation states the DEGREE of kinship between the couple, which the Church computed before it would dispense - second degree equal lateral is first cousins, third is second cousins, and 'with attingency to the second' is two blood paths at once. *** That constrains a pedigree where no parent is written down. ***
how_it_was_caught: *** BY OPENING NINE OF THEM INSTEAD OF ONE. *** The first entry read, on 8 October, was a plain banns dispensation and said nothing either way; the expectation survived because it was never tested against a second.

what_was_said: *** That ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA LARRIERA married Adolfo Cordero at Montevideo on 28 FEBRUARY 1901. *** Carried in her register row since 14 September, from an index.
what_is_true: *** THE ACT SAYS 28 FEBRUARY 1904. *** Same day, same month, three years later. *** THE BOOK DECIDES IT: *** the register is *** La Union, Montevideo, Religious Marriage Records 1902-1934 ***, so a 1901 marriage cannot be in it, and the entry immediately above this one is dated *** May 1902 ***. *** AND IT MAKES SENSE OF THE DISPENSATION: *** the Vicar General lifted their consanguinity impediment on *** 1 February 1901 *** - they were cleared to marry three years before they did. *** A SECOND DISCREPANCY IS RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED: *** the act makes her *** twenty *** in February 1904, which means born about 1883-84, where this register has her born *** 4 November 1880 ***. Both stand.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY FULL-TEXT SEARCH ON HER FORENAMES, after the dispensation ledger turned out to name no parents. *** The ledger entry found yesterday gave the impediment and the date it was lifted; *** the act gives four parents, two ages, two nationalities, a profession and an address ***, and confirms the ledger's wording of the impediment word for word.

what_was_said: *** That JUAN BERNARDO LERENA PELAEZ and the JUAN LERENA of the 1894 dispensation were DIFFERENT PEOPLE. *** Declared in data/_person-pairs.txt earlier the same day: 'Juan LERENA (m. Eduviges Pelaez 1894) is known from ONE LINE of the Montevideo dispensation register and nothing else - with no age, no birth and no parents.' The register carried two rows.
what_is_true: *** THEY ARE ONE MAN. *** The baptism of 26 November 1905 at Santisima Trinidad names the parents the dispensation ledger withheld: 'hijo legitimo de Juan Lerena y Eduviges Pelaez. *** Abuelos paternos: BERNABE y CASIMIRA PELAEZ ***'. Juan Bernardo Lerena Pelaez, born 20 August 1871, is the only Juan among the children of Bernabe Lerena and Casimira Pelaez. *** HE WAS TWENTY-TWO WHEN HE WAS DISPENSED. *** The rows are merged.
how_it_was_caught: Searching the full text for the BRIDE rather than the groom, then looking for a CHILD rather than a marriage - the same method that answered the 1913 couple an hour earlier. *** THE SPLIT WAS NOT BAD REASONING; THE EVIDENCE ARRIVED A DAY LATE. *** What it shows is that 'no parents are recorded' is a statement about a ledger, never about a man.

what_was_said: *** That the Arquidiocesis de Montevideo MARRIAGE DISPENSATION RECORDS are the Vicar General's SUMMARY LEDGER, one sentence per couple, naming no parents - and that the INFORMACIONES MATRIMONIALES are 'a separate series' this archive had not reached. *** Published 8-9 October on /uruguay/ and in data/montevideo-dispensations-fulltext.tsv, itself a correction of an earlier claim that the dispensations DO name parents.
what_is_true: *** THE COLLECTION CONTAINS BOTH, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE DECADE, NOT THE SERIES. *** The volumes read on 8 October were all 1885-1913 and are indeed a summary ledger. *** THE VOLUMES OF THE 1850s IN THE SAME COLLECTION ARE FULL EXPEDIENTES: *** petition, numbered interrogatory, sworn depositions naming parents AND grandparents of both parties, the Cura Vicario's report - and, on the Bernabe Lerena expediente of *** 15 February 1858 ***, *** A KINSHIP DIAGRAM THE PRIEST DREW HIMSELF. *** Three were read on 9 October (1854, 1855, 1858) and all three name four generations.
how_it_was_caught: By doing what the ledger finding said was pointless: searching the dispensation collection for a woman whose parents were wanted. *** THE ORIGINAL CLAIM WAS TRUE OF EVERY VOLUME THIS ARCHIVE HAD OPENED AND FALSE AS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE COLLECTION *** - a generalisation from one date range, published as a fact about a record class. *** IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE SOUTH AFRICA ERROR OF THE DAY BEFORE: *** a true observation about what was tried, written down as a conclusion about what exists.

what_was_said: *** That the 1837 San Jose marriage act and the 1858 Trinidad expediente give the SAME PLACE OF ORIGIN *** - published hours earlier in data/trinidad-founding-kindred.tsv, on /uruguay/ and in the register row for Ramon LERENA of Rosario-Colla, as corroboration for identifying the Colla Ramon with the Ramon of the Trinidad kinship diagram: 'same names, same generation, same place of origin'.
what_is_true: *** THEY GIVE DIFFERENT BIRTHPLACES. *** The 1837 act, read off the plate, says Mauricio Lerena was '*** natural de la VILLA DEL COLLA ***'. The 1858 expediente says the Trinidad Lerenas are '*** naturales de SAN JOSE ***'. *** WHAT IS ACTUALLY SHARED IS NARROWER: *** Mauricio was *** MARRIED *** at San Jose de Mayo and they were *** BORN *** there. The identification loses one of the two legs it was standing on.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY DOING THE TEST THE CLAIM ITSELF NAMED. *** The row said the weakness was that the 1837 act was 'INDEXED, not image-read' and set reading the plate as the test. The plate was read the same day and corrected the paragraph instead of confirming it. *** THE ERROR WAS WRITING A CONCLUSION FROM AN INDEX FIELD ('Birthplace: Colla') WITHOUT NOTICING IT CONTRADICTED THE SENTENCE BEING BUILT *** - the index said Colla all along, on the very page that was being cited.

what_was_said: *** That Cipriano LERENA of Trinidad and Cipriano LERENA Montana were two people. *** Carried as separate register rows since 21 September; the second row itself noted the forename 'is also one of the Trinidad men' and held them apart at index level.
what_is_true: *** ONE MAN. *** The Flores birth act of his daughter Carmen Donata, 2 March 1895 at El Tala, has him declare in person at forty-two, names his wife *** LAUREANA BELOQUI *** and his parents *** MAURICIO [LERENA] and CASIMIRA MONTANO ***. *** THAT IS THE SPOUSE AND BOTH PARENTS IN ONE ACT. *** The rows are merged, and three children already in this register become grandchildren of Mauricio Lerena of Colla.
how_it_was_caught: Searching the full text for the grandmother's name, CASIMIRA MONTANO, rather than for either Cipriano. *** THE PAIR WAS CORRECTLY FLAGGED AND CORRECTLY NOT MERGED FOR EIGHTEEN DAYS ***, which is the system working: it was waiting for an act, and an act came.

what_was_said: *** That the identification of the Trinidad kindred's RAMON LERENA with the RAMON LERENA of Rosario-Colla was an OPEN CANDIDATE, 'NOT MERGED', resting on a name match. *** Published twice on 9 October - in data/trinidad-founding-kindred.tsv, data/colla-trinidad-bridge.tsv, two register rows and two sections of /uruguay/ - with a test proposed and a caution that 'two couples can share two names'.
what_is_true: *** THIS ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY MADE THE IDENTIFICATION ON 17 SEPTEMBER, AND SAID SO IN ITS OWN FILES. *** data/ramon-lerena-rosario.tsv states outright: '*** Bernabe is Alejandro's son; Cipriano is Mauricio's; Alejandro and Mauricio are brothers ***', draws the whole descent from Ramon Lerena and Maria Josefa Gonzalez, and names six of Alejandro's children including BERNABE and SOCORRO. data/descent-spines.tsv carries Ramon's house as a graded *** Documented *** spine, and /uruguay/ has been drawing it for three weeks.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY SEARCHING THE INDEX FOR 'ANY RECORD NAMING RAMON WITH MORE THAN ONE CHILD' - the test this archive set itself - AND FINDING ITS OWN ANSWER FILE. *** *** THE FAILURE WAS NOT READING THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN DATA BEFORE PUBLISHING A WEAKER CLAIM THAN IT ALREADY HELD. *** *** IT IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE PATTERN *** - the 1891 Northam census and the FreeBMD death sweep were both reported as undone when they were done. *** EACH TIME THE CLAIM WAS WRITTEN FROM MEMORY WHILE FINISHING SOMETHING ELSE, AND EACH TIME A FILE IN data/ ALREADY HELD THE ANSWER. ***

what_was_said: *** That BERNABE LERENA of Trinidad was unattached - 'Nothing joins him to these two, and the forename is not proof' *** (register row), and that a third Bernabe 'sits in this register unattached'. Carried in the register since 20 September.
what_is_true: *** THE REGISTER WAS CONTRADICTING THE ARCHIVE'S OWN EVIDENCE FILES FOR THREE WEEKS. *** data/ramon-lerena-rosario.tsv had him as Alejandro's son since 17 September and /uruguay/ drew it; the register said unattached. *** BOTH ARE NOW SUPERSEDED BY DOCUMENTS READ ON 9 OCTOBER *** - his own marriage expediente of 15 February 1858, which names his parents and carries the priest's kinship diagram, and his father's marriage act of 16 September 1825, read off the plate.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY THE REGISTER AND THE EVIDENCE FILES BEING COMPARED FOR THE FIRST TIME. *** This is the defect the owner's question - 'is all this research making it to our sites, persons, families charts, diagrams?' - was pointing at, asked twice. *** THE ANSWER WAS NO IN A DIRECTION NOBODY CHECKED: *** not the register falling behind the site, but *** THE REGISTER FALLING BEHIND data/ ***, with the site rendering the newer of the two and the register rendering the older, both on the same deploy.

what_was_said: *** That lot 210 of Nuno Fernando Lerena's deeds folio lies in 'LONDON STREET'. *** Published hours earlier in data/south-africa-fulltext-closed.tsv, on /south-africa/, in his register row and in work-list row 197 - read off the plate at a magnification that was not enough, and then built on.
what_is_true: *** THE PLATE READS 'LENDIN', NOT 'LONDON'. *** At full magnification the second letter is an unmistakable *** e ***, not an o, and there is an *** n *** before the d where London has none; the i-dot sits after the d. *** THE STREET IS NOT CONFIDENTLY READ *** and is now recorded as 'Lendin (so written; not resolved)'. *** IT IS NOT DEMONSTRABLY 'LEIDEN' EITHER ***, although that is the likeliest intended name - Nuno lived at *** 24 Leiden Road *** - because Leiden would put the i before the d and this hand does not.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY CHECKING THE STREET AGAINST THE PLACE INSTEAD OF ACCEPTING IT. *** Gerdview's streets are named for Dutch and German cities - Leiden, Weert, Cologne - and 'London' did not fit the scheme, which sent the plate back for a harder look. *** THE LESSON IS THE MAGNIFICATION: *** the first read was done at a zoom that resolved 'Lerena' and 'Nuno' perfectly and was still too coarse for a six-letter word in the same hand. *** A READING IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE SMALLEST THING IT RESTS ON. ***

what_was_said: *** That the Lerena cards of army drawer CAJON 985 were 'sitting unread', and that the drawer is 'filed alphabetically'. *** Both published on /open-questions/ under *** question 1, the question this archive exists to answer ***, since 10 September 2026 - a page whose stated purpose is 'published so strangers can help'.
what_is_true: *** THE DRAWER WAS READ ON 10 SEPTEMBER, THE SAME DAY THE QUESTION WAS WRITTEN, AND THE FATHERS TRACED ON THE 13TH. *** data/cajon-985-scan.tsv holds all 39 frames, images 650-688, with every card's indexed parents; data/cajon-985-origins.tsv traces the fathers to three Uruguayan branches. *** AND IT IS NOT ALPHABETICAL: *** the same file records that the drawer is *** GROUPED BY SOUND *** - Lera, Lerena, Lorena, Serena, Sera, Era, Leza, Perena, Perella and Hereijo interfiled - which is a finding in its own right and the reason the index's manglings survived in it. *** TWENTY LERENA CARDS, AND NO JUAN CARLOS ON ANY OF THEM. ***
how_it_was_caught: *** BY GOING TO DO THE WORK THE PAGE ASKED FOR AND FINDING IT DONE. *** *** THIS IS THE WORST PLACE IN THE ARCHIVE FOR IT TO HAVE HAPPENED: *** /open-questions/ exists so that a stranger can help, and its first question was sending them to a drawer that had been read, by a filing rule that is wrong. *** IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE REGISTER CALLING BERNABE UNATTACHED *** - a page that stopped where data/ went on - and the fifth instance recorded today.

what_was_said: *** That the four untraced fathers of Cajon 985 include 'the RAMON of the Concordia pair'. *** Written into /open-questions/ question 1 an hour earlier, when its ask was rewritten.
what_is_true: *** THE CONCORDIA RAMON IS TRACED. *** data/cajon-985-origins.tsv has NEMESIO RAMON LERENA married at *** SALTO, URUGUAY, 16 January 1903 ***, then at Concordia, Entre Rios, directly across the river - one of the three branches the same paragraph calls traced. *** THE FOURTH UNTRACED FATHER IS ARTURO LERENA ***, husband of Amalia Diaz, with sons born in La Pampa, Mendoza and Entre Rios 1889-1897.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY GOING TO SEARCH THE FOUR AND FINDING ONE OF THEM ALREADY ANSWERED. *** The same move that caught the drawer, one level down. *** AND ARTURO IS THE ONE OF THE FOUR THAT THIS ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY GOT WRONG ONCE: *** his row was first written as 'Montevideo 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel' and withdrawn the same day as a conflation with JUAN ARTURO LERENA TRAIBEL, whose wife was Ema Regules. *** A NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY MISIDENTIFIED ONCE DESERVES THE MOST CARE, NOT THE LEAST. ***

what_was_said: *** Three conclusions published on 10 October from a FamilySearch session that had silently SIGNED ITSELF OUT. *** (1) that LEANDRO LORENA and LLANOS are absent from the index, recorded as a *** CONTROLLED NULL ***; (2) that CONCEPCION LERENA is absent; and (3) a method finding that *** a parent-pair query and a spouse-pair query reach two different index shapes ***, built on a clean 0 Results for Carlos Lerena and Adela Carniglia. All three went into data/false-zeros.tsv, data/cajon-985-origins.tsv, /open-questions/ and a commit.
what_is_true: *** THE SESSION WAS SIGNED OUT AND THE PAGE SAID SO IN ONE LINE AT THE TOP: *** 'Create a free account or sign in to see all available results.' *** A SIGNED-OUT SEARCH RETURNS A RESTRICTED, FUZZY TIER *** - twenty-one rows of United States census for every query, whatever the constraint. *** THE PROOF IS THE CONTROL ITSELF: *** the Carniglia spouse-pair query, which returned three true hits earlier the same day and from which two acts were read off the plate, now returns twenty-one rows and *** NOT ONE CARRYING THE NAME ***. *** SO THE NULLS ARE WITHDRAWN AND THE INDEX-SHAPE FINDING IS WITHDRAWN *** - the 0 it rested on has a simpler explanation.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY GOING BACK FOR ARTURO'S ENTRE RIOS MARRIAGE AND FINDING THE SAME URL RETURNING NOISE THAT HAD RETURNED TRUE HITS AN HOUR BEFORE. *** *** THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD THIS TRAP, AS DISGUISE SEVENTEEN: 'THE SESSION THAT LOGGED ITSELF OUT AND DID NOT SAY SO'. *** *** THE CONTROL WAS RUN BEFORE THE NULL AND NOT AFTER IT ***, which is the whole lesson: on a service that can change state mid-session, a control is only evidence if it is re-run AFTER the null it is meant to protect. *** WHAT SURVIVES: *** everything read OFF A PLATE - Carlos Lerena natural de Montevideo, Arturo Lerena Garcia, the Valparaiso act - because those are transcriptions of images, not search results.

what_was_said: *** That of the Lerena fathers in army drawer Cajon 985 whose origin can be traced, 'EVERY ONE is Uruguayan or married in Uruguay'. *** Published in data/cajon-985-origins.tsv since 13 September, strengthened on 9 October when CARLOS LERENA was added as a Montevidean, and leaned on in /open-questions/ question 1 as a *** BASE RATE *** - that an Argentine Lerena of this generation is a Uruguayan family's son far more often than not, and that Juan Carlos Lerena, absent from Rosario, fits that shape.
what_is_true: *** ARTURO LERENA IS SPANISH AND HIS WIFE IS PERUVIAN. *** The marriage of his son Antonio at Crespo, Entre Rios, on 24 October 1924 - a printed form with a nationality blank for each parent - reads '*** hijo de ARTURO LERENA, de nacionalidad ESPANOLA, de profesion PERIODISTA, y de AMALIA DIAZ, de nacionalidad PERUANA ***'. *** FIVE FATHERS ARE NOW TRACEABLE AND THE GENERALISATION FAILS ON THE FIFTH. *** What survives is the weaker statement: *** none of the five is Argentine. *** *** AND THE INFERENCE ABOUT JUAN CARLOS MUST WEAKEN TO MATCH *** - a drawer containing a Spaniard and a Peruvian is a drawer of immigrants, not a drawer of Uruguayans.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY WORKING THE ONE FATHER THE PATTERN HAD NOT YET BEEN TESTED ON. *** The claim was made on three men, restated on four, and broke on the fifth. *** THAT IS WHAT A BASE RATE BUILT ON A HANDFUL DOES ***, and this archive wrote it as a pattern rather than as a count. *** THE HONEST FORM WAS ALWAYS AVAILABLE: 'three of three', not 'every one'. ***

what_was_said: *** That ENRIQUE CARLOS, son of CONCEPCION LERENA, was born at MENDOZA in 1899. *** Carried in data/cajon-985-origins.tsv since 13 September from the FamilySearch index, which gives his birthplace as 'Capital, Mendoza, Argentina'.
what_is_true: *** THE CARD SAYS 'CAP. FEDERAL' - BUENOS AIRES. *** Read off the plate on 10 October 2026: 'LERENA ENRIQUE CARLOS... nacido en *** Cap. Federal ***'. *** THE INDEXER EXPANDED 'CAPITAL' INTO THE WRONG CAPITAL ***, and this archive copied it. *** TWO OTHER THINGS ON THE SAME CARD WERE ALSO INDEXED WRONG: *** the surname is *** LERENA ***, in his own signature, where the index says SERENA; and the index gives him a father, 'Spouses Carlos', where *** THE CARD'S FATHER FIELD IS STRUCK THROUGH WITH A PEN ***, the indexer having taken CARLOS from the son's own forename.
how_it_was_caught: *** BY OPENING THE CARD INSTEAD OF TRUSTING THE INDEX ROW THAT DESCRIBED IT. *** Three errors in one index entry, and this archive had copied one of them into its own file for four weeks. *** THE CARD IS A FINGERPRINT FICHA IN A DIFFERENT DRAWER FROM CAJON 985 ***, which is why it had never been opened: it was reached through the person, not through the drawer.
